final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition of Credit Suisse, with CHF 50 billion SNB emergency liquidity deployed Monday morning, equity written down first, AT1 subordinated, and a coordinated Sunday evening announcement (contract filing 4 PM, SNB statement 5 PM, CS client alerts 5:10 PM) to stabilize confidence before market open.
minority_objections: Wealth client and AT1 rep repeatedly warned that Sunday announcement timing and script execution risk could fail to stop deposit flight if AT1 holders don't trust relationship manager calls before official SNB confirmation
key_conflicts: Sunday evening announcement timing vs Monday 7 AM: CS CEO and clients pushed for Sunday to stop weekend bleed; FINMA initially resisted premature political exposure

AT1 par value protection vs haircut risk: AT1 rep and wealth client demanded explicit commitment that AT1 survives at par if losses exceed equity; Federal Council/FINMA only committed to hierarchy, not value protection
Statement release timing vs deposit spike risk: tension over whether to hold 5 PM announcement if 4-4:45 PM window shows outflows, resolved by SNB authority to accelerate to 4:30 PM
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to Sunday evening announcement (initially resisted) after UBS and clients made clear Monday-only timing would fail to stop deposit flight
FINMA agreed to public contract filing at 4 PM Sunday (before statement) to give AT1 holders written proof of waterfall hierarchy
SNB agreed to accelerate statement to 4:30 PM if deposit outflows exceed CHF 300 million during 4-4:45 PM window
UBS agreed to sign merger framework Friday night (not Sunday morning) to enable Sunday announcement credibility
red_lines: UBS: no signature without equity-first waterfall and CHF 50bn collateral cap locked in binding legal text by Friday midnight
Federal Council: no unlimited state loss protection or guarantees to UBS—creditors bear restructuring risk beyond liquidity support
SNB: CHF 50bn exposure capped at collateral value, not contingent loss absorption if CS losses exceed equity
FINMA: no Sunday announcement unless merger framework signed Friday night—'acquisition is signed' must be legally defensible
AT1 rep: contract must be publicly filed by 4 PM Sunday with explicit equity-first language, or creditor litigation risk kills post-close confidence
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Actual hold rate of AT1 holders during 4-5 PM Sunday window: rehearsals tested script delivery but not whether clients actually commit to waiting 60 minutes before moving money
Leak risk of SNB statement text between 3:45 PM (CS receives it) and 4 PM (calls begin): room assumed script lockdown would work but no enforcement mechanism discussed

Parliamentary backlash risk if CHF 50bn deploys and CS losses later exceed equity write-down: Federal Council gave one-sentence political defense but no scenario planning for post-close loss discovery

Litigation risk from AT1 holders if 'equity written down in full' language is later interpreted to allow UBS due diligence carveouts: FINMA added clarifying sentence but no discussion of enforceability or challenge surface
downstream_risk_variables: Whether AT1 holders actually hold deposits during 4-5 PM Sunday window after relationship manager calls
Whether SNB statement at 5 PM is seen as credible solution or temporary triage by Monday market participants
Whether UBS due diligence post-close reveals losses exceeding equity write-down, triggering AT1 restructuring and creditor backlash
Whether Parliament accepts Federal Council's political defense of CHF 50bn deployment when questioned Monday
Whether Sunday evening announcement sequence (filing 4 PM, statement 5 PM, client alerts 5:10 PM) executes without leaks or technical failures
uncertainty_notes: The room locked the legal architecture (waterfall, collateral cap, merger framework signature) and the Sunday announcement sequence, but left three critical uncertainties unresolved: (1) whether AT1 holders will actually hold deposits for 60 minutes between 4 PM calls and 5 PM statement, despite rehearsals showing script delivery but not client commitment; (2) whether the market reads the Sunday announcement as a done deal or still-pending negotiation, given no discussion of how media/analysts will interpret the timing; (3) whether post-close UBS due diligence reveals losses that trigger AT1 restructuring, exposing the room's assumption that equity write-down would be sufficient.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council R2: 'creditors and capital holders face the restructuring'—liquidity alone insufficient, merger with creditor burden-sharing required. Drove the equity-first waterfall decision.
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS CEO R3: 'We sign—but only if that waterfall is in a binding legal instrument tonight.' UBS acquisition became the binding solution path; signature Friday night was the execution gate.
marker_evidence.government_support: SNB R3: 'CHF 50 billion deploys Monday morning as a federal liquidity loan against collateral.' Government liquidity backstop was the non-negotiable foundation enabling the merger.
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client R5: 'deposits keep flowing out all weekend' unless Sunday announcement happens. Deposit flight risk forced the Sunday evening announcement decision over FINMA's initial Monday-only preference.
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 rep R9: 'does the legal text say equity shareholders written down in full before AT1 absorbs any loss?' AT1 write-down risk drove FINMA's addition of explicit equity-first language to the filed contract.
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep and wealth client repeatedly raised equity vs AT1 hierarchy and par value protection, but the room only locked the sequence (equity first, then AT1), not the value outcome—discussed extensively but did not change the core decision beyond clarifying language.
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep R7: 'you get creditor litigation the moment the merger closes' if contract not filed Sunday. Drove the 4 PM public filing requirement, but did not alter the waterfall or merger terms themselves.
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Federal Council R1: 'we need Federal Council confirmation in writing before market open.' Time pressure to lock legal authority, merger signature, and announcement by Friday night/Sunday drove the entire decision sequence and concessions on Sunday timing.
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Wealth client R1: 'I'm moving my assets Monday morning before the market opens.' Monday panic risk was raised repeatedly as context for urgency, but the actual decision drivers were the Sunday announcement timing and legal instrument deadlines—Monday risk motivated speed but did not dictate specific terms.
